concepts.def: Local Area Network: covers a small geographic area such as a home, school or office.
Wide Area Network: spans large distances, connecting LANs, e.g., the internet.
Network model where clients request services from centralised servers.
Network model where all computers have equal status and share resources directly.
Seven-layer conceptual framework: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.
Unit of data sent over a network, containing header (addresses) and payload (data).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Computer Networks — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Computer Networks brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Computer Networks.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many layers are in the OSI model?
Which describes a network in a single building?
options: WAN
MAN
LAN
PAN

mcqs.q: What is hexadecimal A in denary?
options: Any item, randomly.
26 (A's position in the alphabet).
1 (treating A as the first letter).

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: Any item, randomly.
The computer crashes.
The first one added (FIFO).
The most recently added (top) - LIFO.

mcqs.q: What happens when 11111111 + 1 is computed in an 8-bit register?
options: The computer crashes.
It just becomes 100000000 normally.
Any item, randomly.
Overflow - the result requires 9 bits but only 8 are available.
